lens_summary: Linking/association on the x138 base. Main findings: (1) In x138 the ILP edge set is thrown away. filter_output_graph sets `edges = motion_edges` (exp56 cell 5, lines ~1947-1952). The final links come from a per-frame flow-prior Hungarian with cost = motion residual - 1.0*prob. It has no no-link cost, so any pair inside the gate is forced. It is one-to-one, so every fork comes from the capped safe-division stage. Readmit and gapfill use an UNREFINED low-detection dump on the 1.625 um grid (cell 4 'lowdet peaks' patch). (2) On the LB the whole association layer is worth about +-0.002. Relink off, bonus 2.5 and gshift all gave 0.945 vs 0.947. Min-track 4 and 8 gave 0.943 and 0.944. Seven tail knobs were all flat. (3) The large FN classes are NOT linking errors. Swap, diverted and taken total ~3,600 FN with an oracle of +0.03-0.046. They are node-position/detection errors (l6_fn_anatomy_report.md sec. 3), and a 2x2 swap rule measured -0.00004. Linking-only ceilings from the exp39 anatomy: breaks +0.0011; linefit-displaced nodes +0.005 (oracle); fragments/free-end gaps +0.0087 (oracle upper bound, overlapping); divisions (the only lever with a >= +0.005 arithmetic ceiling) up to +0.015 if every steal-reachable division were found at precision 1 (guess-based decomposition of J_pub 0.36). (4) Part of the head's gain is probably the node multiplier. Final nodes fall by 2.4-2.9%, worth up to +0.0024..+0.0029 via 0.1*dN/N_est at N_pred ~ N_est, and less if N_pred << N_est. So 'better positions feed the association' is real but smaller than +0.007. (5) Honest ceiling of this lens: expected public +0.002..+0.004 for all four ideas together, best case ~+0.01 (mostly divisions). 0.99 (+0.04) is unreachable by association changes. That would need the detection and localisation errors fixed at the source (retrained detector/head), where the swap and a_never oracles (+0.03-0.05) live. The single most useful move under this lens is the CPU 'x138-tail lab' (H3). It is buildable from the existing 199-video head captures, and without it none of the association ideas can be validated honestly before an LB slot.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: x138's +0.007 over readmit-v1 (and exp51's +0.002 over exp48) is localisation that the post-ILP chain converts into edges.
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: The head also shrinks the final node set by 2.4-2.9%. With the adjusted-edge multiplier (1 - 0.1*(N_pred-N_est)/N_est), that alone is worth up to 0.1*0.029 = +0.0029 at N_pred ~ N_est. On our base the whole head gain (+0.002) is therefore explainable by node count, which would make its localisation effect ~0 there. A forum user reported that LB changes tracked the predicted node count.

hypotheses.title: Division slots inside the flow-prior relink (split-aware assignment with a flow-compensated sister-midpoint test)
hypotheses.mechanism: On x138 every final edge comes from a one-to-one Hungarian (motion_relink_edges), so a dividing parent keeps one daughter. The second daughter is either orphaned or, more often, taken by a neighbouring track. Forks are then added only by add_safe_divisions_postlink, which starts from orphans and is capped at 0.375% of nodes per video and 0.76% per frame. The lab funnel (B32) is: orphan-only candidate reach 58/151 GT divisions (38%), steal reach 97/151 (64%), all three nodes detected 121/151 (80%). The pipeline finds 23-25/151 (lab J 0.10-0.12); public J_div ~0.36. The forum confirms that the relink destroys ILP forks and that the second daughter arc needs ~2x the continuation gate (division step 4.57 um vs 1.72 um). Head coordinates make a geometric division test sharper: the two daughters' midpoint should sit at the flow-predicted parent position (parent + neighbourhood flow), while a neighbour-steal does not. This test uses positions and the neighbourhood flow, not network confidence, which is the class of change that transferred best (insertion: lab +0.0019 -> LB +0.001).
hypotheses.change: In exp56 cell 5 motion_relink_edges, after the final tight pass of each frame (flow present), add a division pass. For each matched source s -> d1, the candidates are targets d2 at t+1 within 2 x flow_tight (14 um) of s + flow(s) that are either unmatched or matched from a source s' whose own flow residual is > r_steal (e.g. 3 um) and that can be re-served by an unmatched target within gate (steal with repair). Score = |(d1+d2)/2 - (s+flow(s))| (sister midpoint residual) + w*| |d1-d2| - 8.9 um | + penalty lambda, with hard gates 5 <= |d1-d2| <= 14 um, cos(d1-s, d2-s) <= -0.25, and both steps 2-7 um. Solve per frame as a Hungarian over (sources x second-child columns) with a no-division column at cost lambda; lambda sets the fork count. Keep the DeepCenter safe-div veto (0.25) and the global/frame caps as hard limits, and mark the edges division=1 so the division-geometry filter keeps them. Ship it as a new tools/build_probe_kernel.py patch on --base x138 (the base currently allows only divinsert|leafprune) with ENABLE=0 byte-identical. If #35 (x138 + DaughterNet insertion) wins, run the pass before the insertion and let the insertion's steal skip parents that already have a fork.

hypotheses.title: Global tracklet gap-closing LAP (u-track style, flow-extrapolated, g <= 3) before the short-track filter
hypotheses.mechanism: x138 closes gaps in three greedy local stages: close_single_frame_gaps (1-frame, synthetic midpoint), recover_strict_gap2, and the gapfill (g <= 3, only through free sub-threshold peaks >= 0.5, ALLOW_SYNTHETIC 0, <= 3% added nodes). The short-track filter (min len 6) then deletes any fragment still unlinked. Lab anatomy of exp39: a_tail = 606 FN, where a node within 7 um existed but the tail removed it (mostly the short-track filter); b_break = 150; 424 detection-side FN whose matched end is a free track end/start. The LB rejects lowering the filter (min len 4 gave -0.002) and raising it (8 gave -0.001), so fragments are a mix of junk and real cells. The only way to keep the real ones is to link them into long tracks. A single global assignment over all end(t) -> start(t+1+g) pairs uses the extrapolation of the neighbourhood flow field summed over the gap. With head coordinates its costs are more accurate than greedy per-(t,g) Hungarians, and it lets real fragments survive the filter.
hypotheses.change: After flow relink + readmit + relink (before close_single_frame_gaps), build tracklets. Solve ONE LAP per video over ends x starts with g in 0..3. Cost = |start - (end + sum of per-frame flow medians over g+1 frames)| / sqrt(g+1) + c_g*g. The no-link cost (diagonal) is set so that the gate is ~5 um at g=0 and ~7 um at g=3. Also require a direction test with the tracklets' own last/first velocity (cos >= -0.25, as gapfill CONTEXT does). This is the u-track gap-closing matrix, implementable in ~150 lines with scipy linear_sum_assignment, or with laptrack (BSD-3, pure python; the wheel must be vendored as a Kaggle dataset because kernels have no internet). Fill missing frames with a free low-det peak within 3.5 um of the interpolated point, else a synthetic interpolated node. Keep the existing DeepCenter gap veto (0.25) on synthetic points, and cap synthetic nodes at 1-2% of nodes to protect the node multiplier. Then run the existing gap1/gap2/gapfill (now mostly idle), safe divisions, and the short-track filter. Ship as a --base x138 patch with ENABLE=0 byte-identical.

hypotheses.title: CPU x138-tail lab with head coordinates, then a pre-registered re-tune of the position-consuming association knobs (flow gate, velocity/flow fusion, forward-backward consensus, linefit)
hypotheses.mechanism: The head's value appears only through the post-ILP chain: +0.007 on x138's tail vs +0.002 on ours, with identical pre-ILP coordinates. Every association knob of that chain was tuned by thtennant on integer-grid positions before the head existed. That covers the flow tight gate 7.0, RAW_COST 0, readmit radius 4, gapfill radius 3.5, linefit weight 0.8/window 2, and the velocity weight 0.5, which is used only without a field. The old grid meant 1.625 um quantisation, ~1.15 um RMS noise on a frame-to-frame displacement against a 1.8 um median step. That is why the median-of-12 neighbour flow beat each cell's own velocity, and why linefit 0.8 paid. The head changes the noise model (mean shift 0.74 um, max 1.61 um on the dummy test; public-head GT distance 1.70 -> 1.54 um). So the optimal gates, smoothing and predictor mix probably move. We have no lab that runs this chain with head coordinates, so every association idea is currently unvalidatable. The existing 199-video head captures make one buildable on CPU: 4.83M captured peaks with 224-d features; the lab's 4.21M raw ILP nodes are integer-coordinate peaks from the same prediction stack; the head is a 224->32->3 MLP.
hypotheses.change: (a) Lab build, CPU only. hypotheses.title: Apply the V1284 head to the low-detection pool (readmit and gapfill nodes) and give readmit pairs a neutral relink probability
hypotheses.mechanism: x138 refines only above-threshold peaks. Its 'lowdet peaks' patch dumps sub-threshold peaks (>= 0.3) as unrefined int16 on the 1.625 um grid, before the head runs. Readmitted nodes (1,337 on the 4 dummy clips, ~1.1% of 121,777 raw nodes) and gapfill nodes (cap 3%) therefore sit exactly where tracks broke, with pre-head localisation (GT distance 1.70 vs 1.54 um mean).
